key_insight: This paper introduces an anatomy-aware multimodal fusion framework that better captures how laryngopharyngeal tumors invade surrounding structures, improving CT-based T-staging prediction. By combining CT scans with radiology reports, it aims to make staging more accurate and clinically useful without relying on invasive biopsy alone.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of predicting laryngopharyngeal cancer T-stage from CT images, where tumor invasion patterns are complex and often poorly modeled by existing methods. It also tackles the limitation that prior approaches do not sufficiently use anatomical structure or complementary text information from radiology reports.
method: Uses an anatomy-aware fusion strategy to model fine-grained structural relationships in tumor invasion.
Combines multimodal inputs from CT scans and radiology reports to enrich clinical context.
Learns localized and structured features rather than relying only on whole-volume CT representation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how domain knowledge about anatomy can improve multimodal medical prediction tasks. It is a strong example of designing models that integrate imaging and text to support more accurate, clinically relevant decision-making.

paper_title: Anatomy-aware Fine-grained Multimodal Fusion for Laryngopharyngeal Cancer T-Staging Prediction Using CT and Radiology Report
paper_authors: Xingyue Zhao, Yanzhou Su, Fang Zhang, Zhanghexuan Ji, Yirui Wang
